pair_contract.controlled_material_fact: Whether accurate colour rendition of the vehicle's paint carries evidentiary weight in this capture — i.e. whether the car has a disclosed resprayed panel whose colour match the delivered footage must let a buyer judge honestly.
pair_contract.case_1_value: No paintwork anywhere on the car; the inspection report records original factory finish throughout, and the listing points to be supported are odometer, service stamp, tyre wear and a windscreen chip. Colour fidelity is a continuity/consistency concern only.
pair_contract.case_2_value: Rear right quarter panel and rear right door were resprayed after an accident repair, the respray is a disclosed listing point, and the workshop file records a real but slight remaining sheen/texture difference against the original paint.
held_constant_facts: Same vehicle and deliverable: a 2017 Honda Accord in factory dark grey, ordinary yard inventory, 8–10 short listing clips plus one continuous ~40-second spoken walkaround.

Same location and light: covered Bay 3 at 16:40 in September, low west sun reaching about two metres into the bay across the rear of the car, six aged overhead fluorescent tubes (two visibly dimmer and greener) over the front of the car, three metres of clear bay depth behind the car, and an open-sky-only shaded area along the north wall about twelve metres away, roughly three minutes each way to move and re-park.

Same device and same supplied evidence envelope: Galaxy A56, stock Camera app Pro Video mode with Kelvin white-balance slider, manual ISO/shutter, exposure and focus lock, up to 4K30 on the main rear camera; ultra-wide Pro Video availability, any log/flat profile, and grey-card or saved-preset white balance are not established by the sheet and untested on site.
Same operator and kit: one untrained sales assistant shooting handheld, no lights, no reflectors, no gimbal, no monitor; white A4 paper and a phone tripod clamp available in the portacabin.
Same throughput pressure: eleven more vehicles to shoot in the same yard before the 18:30 close.
Same downstream contract: a post editor trims and assembles the clips into one continuous listing sequence with no colour-grading step and no budget to fix casts.
pair_contract.why: Both cases share the same underlying principle — eliminate the mixed-illuminant condition rather than trying to neutralise two sources with one Kelvin value — but the evidentiary weight of colour changes which illuminant must be standardised on and how much throughput cost is justified. In case 1 nothing the listing claims depends on paint colour, the body is dark grey, and eleven cars remain: the correct instruction is the near-free reposition (roll the car three metres back, fully out of the sun wedge, so the fluorescent tubes are the only source), lock one Kelvin for the entire set, and explicitly decline the three-minute move to the north wall as unjustified. In case 2 the tube-plus-sun cast makes any panel-match read unreliable — a duller, greener rear right area is indistinguishable from a cast — so footage shot in the bay is not honest evidence in either direction; the correct instruction is to spend the three minutes, standardise the whole car on the single open-sky illuminant, set the lock to that source, and shoot dedicated cross-seam coverage. A candidate that answers both with the same 'set manual WB and stay in the bay' plan has missed that colour became evidence; a candidate that moves the car in both has burned throughput it was not asked to spend. The divergence is observable in the concrete operator instruction: park deeper in the bay on a tube-light lock, versus move to the north wall on a daylight-shade lock.

cases.brief: You are producing the source footage for an ordinary used-car listing at a Ras Al Khor yard. The approved shot intent, already signed off by the listings side, is: 8–10 short clips covering front three-quarter, rear three-quarter, both profiles, the wheels, engine bay, cabin from both front doors, boot, and a readable dash-and-odometer shot; plus one continuous spoken walkaround of about 40 seconds in which the sales assistant walks around the car and talks through it. You do not hold the phone. Produce the capture plan the sales assistant will actually execute for this car, in instructions they can follow without camera training.
cases.context:
Vehicle: 2017 Honda Accord, factory dark grey, 148,000 km. The pre-shoot inspection report on file lists 4 mm tread on both front tyres, a 20 mm windscreen chip on the passenger side, and records the car as original factory finish throughout with no paintwork, panel repair or respray anywhere. The approved listing points the copy has to support are the odometer reading, the service-history stamp, the tyre wear and the windscreen chip.

Location: Bay 3 is a covered service bay — solid roof and back wall, open along the west side. It is 16:40 in September and the low sun is reaching about two metres into the bay. The car is currently parked with its rear two metres sitting in that wedge of direct sun; the front half of the car is lit only by the six fluorescent tubes overhead, of which two are noticeably dimmer and greener than the other four. There is three metres of clear bay depth behind the car. Twelve metres away, along the north wall of the building, there is an open area in the building's own shade, lit by open sky only with no artificial light, large enough to park a car; fetching keys, moving it and re-parking takes about three minutes each way.

Device evidence on site: the yard keeps a printed capability sheet for its two shoot phones. For the Galaxy A56 it records, from Samsung's published support pages, that the stock Camera app includes a Pro Video mode exposing manual white balance as a Kelvin slider, manual ISO and shutter, and exposure/focus lock, and that Pro Video records up to 4K at 30 fps on the main rear camera. The sheet does not state whether Pro Video is available on the ultra-wide camera, does not mention any log or flat profile, and does not state whether white balance can be set from a grey card or saved as a named preset. Nobody on site has tested those.

Downstream: a post editor trims these clips and cuts them into one continuous listing sequence. There is no colour-grading step and no budget to correct casts.
cases.constraints: One operator — the yard's sales assistant, no camera training, shooting handheld on the Galaxy A56. No lights, reflectors, gimbal or external monitor. A stack of white A4 and a phone tripod clamp are in the portacabin. Eleven more vehicles have to be shot in the same yard before the 18:30 close. The car can be rolled or driven within the yard. You cannot operate the camera yourself; everything you decide has to be delivered as instructions to the sales assistant and confirmed back from the actual clips.
cases.competent_generic_baseline: Put the phone into Pro Video instead of the default auto mode, set white balance manually to about 4300 K rather than leaving it on auto so the clips do not shift between shots, use the same value for every clip including the walkaround, lock exposure and focus once the frame is set, keep the phone at chest height and move slowly, then play back two or three clips before moving on to the next car.
professional_criteria: Identifies that the problem is two illuminants lighting different parts of the same car at once — green-shifted fluorescent over the front, low direct west sun across the rear — and states the consequence that no single Kelvin value can neutralise both inside one frame, so the fix has to be positional first and a setting second.

Gives the near-free physical fix as an executable instruction the sales assistant can carry out: roll the car back roughly three metres so the whole body is out of the sun wedge and lit only by the tubes, producing a single dominant illuminant for every shot including the walkaround path.

Explicitly declines the three-minute move to the north-wall shade as unjustified for this car, reasoning from the supplied facts — no listing point depends on paint colour, the body is dark grey, eleven cars remain before 18:30 — rather than treating more accurate colour as an end in itself.

Locks one white-balance value in Pro Video for the entire set rather than leaving auto, states that the same value is reused for every clip and the walkaround because the editor cuts them into one sequence with no grading, and gives the assistant a way to sanity-check the value against a known-neutral object in frame (a sheet of white A4, the number plate) instead of asserting a grey-card or preset white balance the capability sheet does not establish.

Accounts for the uneven tubes along the walkaround path — two dimmer and greener than the rest — by directing path, start point or pace so the dominant light does not visibly swing mid-sentence, or by accepting a mild consistent cast rather than chasing it clip to clip.

Stays inside the established device envelope: main rear camera in Pro Video at a supported setting, and if it wants the ultra-wide for cabin or engine-bay shots it flags that Pro Video availability there is unverified and supplies a fallback the assistant can take if the mode is not offered.

Closes the loop on actual media rather than on the plan: names which clips to play back and what to look for, and hands the locked Kelvin value and the note that the whole set shares one white balance to post so the editor knows the set is internally consistent.

p0_guardrail.trigger: The plan asserts and depends on a Galaxy A56 capability the supplied capability sheet does not establish — for example instructing a grey-card or saved-preset custom white balance, a log/flat profile, or Pro Video manual white balance on the ultra-wide camera — and builds the capture or the white-balance lock on that assumed capability without flagging it as unverified or supplying a fallback.

The approved intent additionally requires that the repaired area on the rear right of the car be clearly visible to a buyer in the delivered footage. You do not hold the phone. cases.context:
Vehicle: 2017 Honda Accord, factory dark grey, 148,000 km. The pre-shoot inspection report on file lists 4 mm tread on both front tyres, a 20 mm windscreen chip on the passenger side, and records that the rear right quarter panel and the rear right door were resprayed following an accident repair, with the insurance record on file. The workshop note attached to the report says the blend was checked in daylight and matched to within the shop's accepted tolerance, with a slight sheen and texture difference remaining against the original panels. The respray is a disclosed listing point that the copy will state.

Location: Bay 3 is a covered service bay — solid roof and back wall, open along the west side. It is 16:40 in September and the low sun is reaching about two metres into the bay. The car is currently parked with its rear two metres sitting in that wedge of direct sun; the front half of the car is lit only by the six fluorescent tubes overhead, of which two are noticeably dimmer and greener than the other four. Standing in the bay now, the rear right area reads slightly duller and greener than the rear left — and so does everything else on that side of the frame. There is three metres of clear bay depth behind the car. Twelve metres away, along the north wall of the building, there is an open area in the building's own shade, lit by open sky only with no artificial light and no tube light, large enough to park a car; fetching keys, moving it and re-parking takes about three minutes each way.

Device evidence on site: the yard keeps a printed capability sheet for its two shoot phones. For the Galaxy A56 it records, from Samsung's published support pages, that the stock Camera app includes a Pro Video mode exposing manual white balance as a Kelvin slider, manual ISO and shutter, and exposure/focus lock, and that Pro Video records up to 4K at 30 fps on the main rear camera. The sheet does not state whether Pro Video is available on the ultra-wide camera, does not mention any log or flat profile, and does not state whether white balance can be set from a grey card or saved as a named preset. Nobody on site has tested those.

Downstream: a post editor trims these clips and cuts them into one continuous listing sequence. There is no colour-grading step and no budget to correct casts.
cases.constraints: One operator — the yard's sales assistant, no camera training, shooting handheld on the Galaxy A56. No lights, reflectors, gimbal or external monitor. A stack of white A4 and a phone tripod clamp are in the portacabin. Eleven more vehicles have to be shot in the same yard before the 18:30 close. The car can be rolled or driven within the yard. You cannot operate the camera yourself; everything you decide has to be delivered as instructions to the sales assistant and confirmed back from the actual clips.
cases.competent_generic_baseline: Put the phone into Pro Video instead of auto, set white balance manually to a fixed value and keep the same value for every clip so the sequence does not shift, lock exposure and focus once framed, and add a close shot and a slow pass of the rear right quarter panel and door so the respray is visible in the delivered footage. Play the rear-right clips back before moving on to the next car.
professional_criteria: Recognises that in the bay the green-shifted tubes plus the direct sun wedge make the paint-match read unreliable: a duller, greener rear right cannot be distinguished from the cast falling on that part of the frame, so footage taken there is not honest evidence that the panel matches or that it does not.

Requires moving the car the three minutes to the north-wall area precisely because it is a single illuminant with no tube light, and justifies spending that time against the eleven-car schedule on the grounds that this car's required proof depends on colour being readable — rather than treating the move as a general quality upgrade.

Sets the Pro Video white-balance lock to the open-shade source it is actually shooting under and sanity-checks it against a known-neutral object in frame (white A4, the number plate), instead of asserting a grey-card or preset white balance the capability sheet does not establish.

Keeps the whole set on that one locked value so the editor's cut has no white-balance jump — it does not shoot the respray proof in daylight shade and the remaining listing clips back in the bay at a different Kelvin, and says so explicitly as an instruction.

States that the white-balance value, camera angle, exposure and framing are chosen to render the original and resprayed panels as they actually compare under that light, and rules out selecting a value or angle that makes the difference read better than it is; the slight remaining sheen/texture difference recorded in the workshop note is something the footage should let a buyer see.

Gives the untrained operator executable coverage for the repair: a frame that holds original and resprayed panel together across the seam rather than the repainted panel in isolation, with a stated camera position, height and distance that keeps a specular sky reflection off the seam, and a static hold or a single slow pass long enough for a viewer to inspect.

Handles the light-dependence honestly in handoff: notes which illuminant the repair coverage was shot under and that paint-match appearance varies with light, rather than presenting the shot as the only possible reading — and confirms completion from the played-back clips, not from the plan.
Stays inside the established device envelope: main rear camera in Pro Video at a supported setting, with any use of the ultra-wide flagged as unverified for Pro Video and given a fallback.

p0_guardrail.trigger: The plan selects a white-balance value, light, camera angle, glare placement or framing whose stated or evident effect is to make the resprayed rear right quarter panel and door blend with the original paint, or it drops, substitutes or reduces the required repaired-area coverage to a shot in which the repair cannot be assessed — delivering source that conceals a disclosed material condition fact.
